entries.sourceClaim: The slide broadly contrasts traditional methods and neural networks without qualifying every method or operating condition.
entries.qualification: The comparison describes tendencies; map requirements, adaptation, computation and performance depend on the specific method and task.

entries.sourceClaim: The surrounding navigation discussion can suggest steering prediction, but this reused CNN figure specifically labels32 waypoint/direction classes.
entries.qualification: The figure ends in32 labeled waypoint/direction classes rather than a single steering-regression output.

entries.sourceClaim: The slide table calls the direction a shortest-path direction; the supplied teacher is a local Manhattan-greedy rule whose success is layout-dependent.
entries.qualification: The helper tests neighboring actions in preference order using Manhattan distance; it does not maintain a graph-search frontier.

entries.sourceClaim: A successful toy-maze demonstration must not be read as evidence of general navigation performance.
entries.qualification: Training accuracy measures agreement on the examples used for training; the other settings require separate evaluation.

entries.sourceClaim: The slide lists advantages and limitations; benefits should not become unconditional robustness or performance claims.
entries.qualification: Neural models can represent nonlinear input-output relations, but performance, robustness and interpretability depend on training and design.

entries.sourceClaim: The table compresses the IMU role into an orientation label; this does not imply perfect absolute orientation or full pose.
entries.qualification: An IMU measures quantities such as angular velocity and acceleration used in state estimation; an orientation estimate is not automatically drift-free absolute pose.
